purpose: Wazuh acceptance test: the scanner against a real Wazuh 4.14.9 indexer with real vulnerability data

environment.docker: Docker Desktop, server 28.0.1, linux/arm64 VM with 8 GiB

setup: Adapted from wazuh-docker v4.14.9 single-node; nothing of it is kept in this repository
Only the indexer (127.0.0.1:9200) and the dashboard (127.0.0.1:443) were published, and only on this Mac
Random passwords replaced the published defaults; the demo accounts (kibanaro, logstash, readall, snapshotrestore) were removed, and the old admin password and readall were refused (401)
Certificates from Wazuh's own certificate tool; the indexer certificate was re-issued from the same key, CA and subject, adding localhost and 127.0.0.1 to its names
Two agents in containers (Amazon Linux 2023), test-agent-one = 001 and test-agent-two = 002; no agent on this Mac, which sent nothing to Wazuh
Scanner account pc-scanner: role allows only 'read' on wazuh-states-vulnerabilities-*, with document-level security {"term": {"agent.id": "001"}}

issue_found.summary: Every request failed on Python 3.13 and later with only 'Wazuh connection or TLS verification failed'
issue_found.cause: ssl.create_default_context() sets VERIFY_X509_STRICT from Python 3.13, and the root CA made by Wazuh's certificate tool has no key usage extension: 'CA cert does not include key usage extension'. Python 3.11 and curl accepted the same CA
issue_found.owner_decision: Relax the strict checks only for the CA the owner sets in wazuh.ca_file; the system certificates keep them. The chain, its dates and the host name are still verified
issue_found.fix: pc_scanner/core.py clears VERIFY_X509_STRICT only with wazuh.ca_file, and a failed verification names OpenSSL's reason. Reproduced first with a test server whose CA is made the same way

paging_and_aggregation.page_size_override: PAGE_SIZE changed to 5 only inside the test process; production default remains 500
paging_and_aggregation.query: The scanner's normal sort (including missing-value handling) and search_after against the real indexer

dashboard.status_explanation: Paged responses are partial individually; aggregation preserves the worst page status even after all pages are fetched

cancellation_timer_race.interpretation: Response completed before the cancellation polling loop could interrupt it; not evidence of successful in-flight cancellation

delayed_real_response.method: A local TCP relay forwarded traffic to the real indexer without decrypting TLS; after the end-to-end TLS handshake, it deliberately held the indexer's response instead of delivering it to the scanner

deadline.error: Wazuh did not finish answering within 1 seconds; search was not completed

cancellation.signal: threading.Event set 0.1 seconds after the relay started holding the response
cancellation.error: Scan cancelled; scan was not completed

limitations: The relay introduced the delay; the real indexer itself was not made slow
The real-indexer test did not isolate a stall after HTTP response headers; that case is covered separately by the controlled TLS-server regression tests
These elapsed times are observations on macOS, not guarantees for Windows or Linux

not_covered: Paging at the production size of 500: the real dataset had only 23 records; multi-page real-indexer behavior was verified with a test-process page size of 5
An agent on this Mac, and so a match with this PC's host name (the agent_name setting was used)
Windows and Linux hosts running the scanner
A naturally slow real indexer or a real-indexer HTTP body stall: deadline and in-flight cancellation were verified by delaying the real response in a TCP relay
